  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  June 17, 2021
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:07 p.m., on Thursday, June 17, 2021 the Alhambra City Council met in person
in Council Chambers and via video conference and teleconference.

PRESENT via tele/video conference: MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
PRESENT:  LEE
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present physically, via teleconference, and via video conference: City Manager
Binnquist, City Attorney Montes, Assistant City Manager Garcia, City Clerk Myles, Director of
Community Development Ho, Principal Planner Lam

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M21-82

The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the City Council
being held this evening pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956
of the Government Code of the State of California.

CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING

1.  APPLICATIONS FOR VESTING TENTATIVE TRACT MAP TT 74194, RESIDENTIAL
  PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT RP-17-7, CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT CU-17-9
  AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE PROPOSED
  VILLAGES AT THE ALHAMBRA PROJECT (PROJECT) WITH 294 NEW, FOR-SALE,
  RESIDENTIAL DWELLING UNITS IN FIVE-STORY STACKED FLAT AND
  TOWNHOME CONFIGURATIONS; 545 NEW RENTAL APARTMENTS IN FIVE-STORY
  STACKED FLAT CONFIGURATIONS; AND UP TO 4,347 TOTAL PARKING SPACES
  TO ACCOMMODATE ALL NEW USES. IT IS EXPECTED THAT IF THE PROJECT IS
  APPROVED THE APPLICANT WILL IMPLEMENT A PARKING REDUCTION
  PURSUANT TO ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 23.52.060. THE PROJECT
  SITE IS LOCATED IN THE PO (PROFESSIONAL OFFICE) ZONE. AN
  ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT HAS BEEN PREPARED FOR THE PROJECT
  AND WILL ALSO BE CONSIDERED WITH THE PROJECT ALONG WITH A POSSIBLE
  STATEMENT OF OVERRIDING CONSIDERATIONS – F2M17-50, N2M20-163

  Community Development HO delivered a staff report on the background of the item and
  the current stage of the project.

  On June 10, 2021, a special meeting of the City Council was held for review of the
  continued public hearing for the application by the Ratkovich Company for the Villages at
  The Alhambra project (“Project”), comprised of a total of 775 residential units, including
  230 for-sale condominiums and 545 for-rent apartment units. A Development Agreement

  1
6-17-21
   is also proposed as part of the Project. The Council Sub-Committee was of the opinion
  that additional time was needed to negotiate the terms of the Development Agreement.
  The additional time would also afford the Applicant the opportunity to complete the revised
  Air Quality Analysis and Level of Service documents for the reduced 775-unit
  development. In light of the Sub-Committee’s indication that additional time was needed
  for negotiations, the Council deferred taking any additional public testimony until the next
  scheduled meeting, and continued the Public Hearing to a special meeting of the City
  Council this evening. The Sub-Committee and Applicant last met on June 10, 2021. Prior
  to that, the Sub-Committee and the applicant met two (2) other times on May 25 and June
  3, 2021 to discuss the Sub-Committee’s concerns. The Sub-Committee will provide the
  Council with more details of their negotiations with respect to density, affordability, soil
  contamination, indemnification language, traffic, trees, stormwater management,
  workforce and open space, after which staff sought direction on working with the Project
  Applicant to revise the draft Development Agreement for further consideration by the City
  Council.

  Additional environmental documents for the 775-unit proposal were also requested by the
  City Council during previous hearings. These documents consisted of a Vehicle Miles
  Traveled (“VMT”) analysis, a revised Air Quality analysis, and a Level of Service (“LOS”)
  analysis. The VMT analysis was completed on May 14, 2021, and was included with this
  evening’s staff report and is on file in the city clerk’s office. The VMT analysis concluded
  the Project’s transportation impacts would be less than significant and no mitigation
  measures are required. The Revised Air Quality analysis was completed on June 15, 2021
  (on file in the City Clerk’s office), and concluded the development of 775 units under the
  revised phasing schedule and revised Mitigation Measure AQ-MM-1 would substantially
  reduce emissions in comparison to the Project as previously evaluated under the Draft
  Environmental Impact Report. The LOS analysis was submitted as of the time the staff
  report was prepared and staff finalized the review of the analysis. A draft copy of the LOS
  analysis was provided as part of the staff report and was also available on the City’s
  website at:

  https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vLnbT4SmQKYfpZDcxLTofXJ8Di4RrT2u/view?usp=sharing.

  Councilmember PÉREZ reported on the meetings held with the Subcommittee to include
  low-income housing and that the developer currently offered that they would increase
  affordable units to 15% of the rental units. She also reported on the “phase in” construction
  process for public input, and provided a schedule of reports to council during each phase
  up to project completion. She also reported on the transportation issues, and stated that
  there was consideration of a transportation hub at the corner of Fremont and Orange in
  cooperation with Los Angeles County and the Southern California Association of
  Governments (SCAG). She stated that they requested the Appellant make a commitment
  to advocate for this transportation hub on behalf of the City, or that they commit to making
  their own transportation hub at the project site if the joint transportation hub project did not
  come to fruition. She also stated that the issue of a local labor agreement with the project
  was still under discussion and that the Ratkovich Company was still negotiating with
  unions.

  Councilmember MALONEY also reported on the Subcommittee meetings and
  acknowledged the efforts of the first subcommittee. He echoed Ms. Pérez’s comments
  regarding the emphasis on affordable housing and transportation. He commented on the

  2
6-17-21
   offers made by the Appellant to mitigate concerns as well as the City’s efforts to mitigate
  traffic issues in the area.

  Ms. PÉREZ also reported on the subcommittee’s meeting with the Regional Water Quality
  Control Board regarding existing concerns about the site. She stated that they would
  review the environmental report, casefile, as well as the use covenant. She stated that an
  update was anticipated by June 28, 2021. Mr. MALONEY also commented on the meeting
  and the Regional Water Quality Control Board’s approach to the site.

  Appellant Rebuttal: Megan MOLOUGHNEY thanked everyone for their comments, and
  urged Council to move forward with approving the project Development Agreement.

RECESS & RECONVENE: Mayor Lee called for a brief recess at 9:15 p.m. and the meeting
resumed with all Councilmembers present at 9:25 p.m.

  Discussion: Council discussed various issues addressed by public comment as well as
  previous topics of discussion. Councilmember MALONEY and Mr. HO discussed the
  public’s concerns regarding the project’s impact on infrastructure and city services. Mr.
  MALONEY, Dennis PASCUA and Nicole COBLEIGH, the city’s consultants from Dudek
  Environmental discussed the impact on local schools and provided an explanation for the
  results as provided by Alhambra Unified School District to the appellant’s consultant
  Kimley-Horn who conducted the EIR.

  Council continued to have an in-depth discussion regarding traffic studies with consultants
  PASCUA and COBLEIGH from Dudek Environmental, Ms. MOLOUGHNEY, Matt
  STEWART from Kimley-Horn the consultants to the Appellant, as well as City Attorney
  MONTES, and Mr. HO. Topics of discussion included the differences between Vehicle
  Miles Traveled (VMT) reports and Level of Service (LOS) reports, the effects of the
  project’s proximity to transportation as a high transit area, the various trip credits for the
  project under the VMT report, the LOS rating for intersections adjacent to the project, the
  metrics used in conducting the LOS and VMT analyses, the role of VMT reports under
  CEQA, the role of the LOS reports in the City’s General Plan guidelines and the City’s
  ability to impose conditions based on the reports, and the traffic impact of Accessory
  Dwelling Units in residential areas.

  Council also discussed the topic of affordable housing with Mr. HO, and Ms.
  MOLOUGHNEY. Mr. MALONEY and Mr. HO discussed the rental rates in the affordable
  units within the project. Ms. PÉREZ and Ms. MOLOUGHNEY discussed the distribution of
  affordable units throughout the rental unit parcel.

  5
6-17-21
   Council addressed environmental concerns with the project. Mr. MAZA and Ms.
  MOLOUGHNEY discussed the cleanup of the site and the rulings issued by the Regional
  Water Quality Control Board which determined that there was closure on the entire site,
  including the North Parcel and Corner Parcel, with deed restrictions. Mayor LEE and Ms.
  MOLOUGHNEY discussed the North Parcel and the Corner Parcel which would have a
  vapor barrier constructed as well as continued testing per the deed restriction issued. Ms.
  PÉREZ reiterated that the Second Subcommittee recently met with the Regional Water
  Quality Control Board who issued guidance to the Ratkovich Company and would issue a
  report expected by June 28, 2021. Ms. LEE, Ms. MOLOUGHNEY, and Tracy EGOSCUE,
  outside environmental counsel for the Ratkovich Company, further discussed any potential
  disclosures of the property site to prospective renters or home owners. Ms. EGOSCUE
  clarified that she helped bring the site to closure with extensive sampling and testing done
  on site. She stated that the requirements to protect human health would be confirmed in
  correspondence from Regional Water Board and that indoor air would have to meet
  highest standards required by State. After the vapor barrier installation, the air would have
  to be sampled and found to be clean. She stated that disclosure would have to be required
  if the air was found not to be clean.

  Council also had ongoing discussions regarding the pending workforce agreement
  between the Ratkovich Company and local labor unions. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and
  Ms. PÉREZ each emphasized the importance of an agreement, based on previous
  Council direction, to ensure the construction of the Villages project utilized local labor
  unions and resident workers. Ms. LEE and Mr. MONTES discussed the labor agreement
  and its role in Council’s decision to approve or deny the project. Ms. MOLOUGHNEY
  clarified that she anticipated the labor agreement being concluded by the next special City
  Council Meeting.

  Council discussed their next course of action and continued to review the previous topics
  of discussion and their impact on the overall decision. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER
  expressed a need for more time to allow for public review of the recent reports, Ms. LEE
  addressed the discrepancy in the former VMT analysis and the current proposed number
  of units, Ms. PÉREZ further addressed the need for the labor agreement and a phase in
  plan with periodic analysis. Council ultimately determined that they would continue the
  public hearing in order to allow for continued public review, receive updates from the
  Appellant on the VMT analysis and updates to other reports, receive staff analysis of
  recently submitted reports, receive communication from the Regional Water Quality
  Control Board regarding their review of recent data, and the conclusion of negotiations for
  a workforce agreement. Ms. LEE requested a motion to approve the item, and received
  no motion or second. Ms. LEE requested a motion to continue the public hearing to a date
  certain in July, which was motioned by Ms. PÉREZ and seconded by Ms. ANDRADE-
  STADLER. After discussion with Mr. MONTES, Council directed staff to prepare a draft
  development agreement for their review at the special meeting, but allowed that they
  would have to prepare the documents and resolutions for either approval or denial of the
  project at a following meeting. Ms. MOLOUGHNEY assured Council that all reports could
  be completed and run parallel to staff’s preparation of a development agreement. Council
  discussed the date for the special meeting and the motion was amended to continue the
  hearing to Tuesday, July 6, 2021 at 6:00 p.m.

  Action Taken:  The City Council took the following actions:

  6
6-17-21
   1.  Received and filed the City Council Sub-Committee negotiation report for the
  Villages at The Alhambra project Development Agreement;
  2.  Took public testimony;
  3.  Directed staff to return with updated reports discussed;
  4.  Directed staff to draft a development agreement for review; and
  5.  Continued the hearing to Tuesday, July 6, 2021 at 6:00 p.m.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded: ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

ADJOURNMENT: At 11:08 p.m., there being no further business for the Council to transact, the
Mayor, with the consent of the City Council, adjourned their meeting.
